newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-MCGRATH STRIKES BEFORE RAIN RETURNS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MCGRATH STRIKES BEFORE RAIN RETURNS.

text.p: Glenn McGrath scythed through the top of the England batting on Friday before rain brought a premature end to the second day of the second test between England and Australia at Lord's.

McGrath, bowling with pace and menace on a responsive pitch, took wickets with the final ball in each of his fourth, fifth and sixth overs to reduce England to 38 for three in the 90 minutes' play possible.
Thursday's scheduled opening day was washed out.
Mark Taylor, needing to force a win within four days to level the six-test Ashes series, immediately asked England to bat after winning the toss on a cool, cloudy morning.
McGrath soon vindicated his decision, bowling to a fuller length than in the nine-wicket defeat at Edgbaston, while Paul Reiffel made the ball move extravagantly down the slope from the Pavilion end.
Mark Butcher, who failed twice in his maiden test at Edgbaston, was rapped twice on the pads by Reiffel, whose loud demand for lbw was turned down both times.
Butcher was also beaten badly by both pacemen outside the off-stump and it was no surprise when he departed for five, popping up a catch from pad and bat to Greg Blewett at short-leg.

England skipper Michael Atherton, who appeared to have a clearer idea where his off-stump was, followed in McGrath's next over, athletically caught for one by Taylor at first slip tumbling low to his right.
Then Alec Stewart, who had also scored only one, decided to shoulder arms to McGrath only to watch dumbfounded as the ball clipped the top of his off-stump.
But Graham Thorpe and Nasser Hussain, who shared a 288-run stand in the first test, eventually saw off McGrath after a spiteful 10 overs costing only 21 runs.
Then the rains came, the covers went on and play was finally called off for the day in mid-afternoon.
England had at least two milestones to celebrate after another desperately disappointing day for the teams and the spectators alike.
Atherton overtook the late Peter May's record of 41 tests as England captain and for the first time since 1991 the home side were unchanged for consecutive tests.
